aelindor.belief: Air Spirits have their own journeys. A bond begins with attention, not a command.
aelindor.place: The Bough Palace governs from a city of woodland courts. Open ground belongs to paths and gathering places as well as to buildings.
aelindor.title: The living court
aelindor.voice: A forest is not empty land waiting for houses. Its clearings already serve a purpose.

briarhaven.belief: A bonded Spirit is a companion with its own will. Worship strengthens your practice; it does not turn that companion into property.
briarhaven.place: The bank, kitchen and market face a shared square. The Magic School teaches Relic shaping beside the gathering country that supplies it.
briarhaven.title: A haven for returning travelers
briarhaven.voice: Firstlight teaches you to survive. Here you decide what to make of those skills. Ask Captain Rellan about the trouble on the northern road.

copperdelve.belief: Earth Spirits are encountered through patient work with stone, not by claiming ownership of a mountain.
copperdelve.place: Small workshops and stores support crews traveling into mineral country. Tools are repaired here before they are replaced.
copperdelve.title: The prospectors’ village
copperdelve.voice: Start with ore you can actually work. A heavier pick does not make an unfamiliar seam safe.

crownreach.belief: We light a candle for those who keep the roads, not only those who rule them.
crownreach.place: Grain levies and road contracts keep Sunspire supplied. Courtyard markets leave the gate approaches clear for arriving caravans.
crownreach.title: The road court
crownreach.voice: Our clerks keep two copies of every road order. A seal is useful; a witness is better.

deepforge.belief: We set aside the first quiet moment after the furnaces cool to remember absent workers.
deepforge.place: Workshop courts and heavy stone halls serve the eastern mineral country. Ore, fuel and finished equipment pass through different hands here.
deepforge.title: The foundry city
deepforge.voice: A smith needs miners and fuel cutters. A fine blade begins long before it reaches my anvil.

fernwatch.belief: Cutting wood and tending what remains are parts of the same responsibility.
fernwatch.place: Rangers and craftspeople share a village at the edge of the southern forest routes. Clear approaches help travelers recognize shelter.
fernwatch.title: The woodland threshold
fernwatch.voice: Thick woodland needs a path, not a cleared hillside. Follow the road until you know the ground.

greyhaven.belief: A traveler may leave an offering for the next traveler without giving a name.
greyhaven.place: Storehouses and market courts gather goods from the western farms before the long roads east. Repair yards matter as much as shopfronts here.
greyhaven.title: The caravan exchange
greyhaven.voice: Count your supplies before you leave. Beyond the town, the Badlands offer fewer safe places to stop.

ironhollow.belief: Remembering the dead does not mean obeying every voice that uses their names.
ironhollow.place: Ironcrown and the mine works share a mountain. Working shafts support the city; the Wardkeepers maintained older chambers beneath them.
ironhollow.title: The city above the seals
ironhollow.voice: Hesta keeps the rescue camp. If you hear a voice in a closed shaft, bring a witness before following it.

moonwillow.belief: We keep remembrance close to living trees; the forest continues after each of us.
moonwillow.place: Woodland homes stand above root caverns. The Brood Hollow makes watching the forest floor as necessary as watching the road.
moonwillow.title: The watch beneath the canopy
moonwillow.voice: The roots hide passages. Do not mistake a quiet cave for an abandoned one.

silverbrook.belief: Water Spirits are companions discovered through fishing. The water is shared even when the bond is yours.
silverbrook.place: The village joins woodland craft with the needs of travelers moving between the elven cities. Water and timber shape its daily work.
silverbrook.title: The waterside craft village
silverbrook.voice: Fishing and crafting reward patience. Bring useful materials home instead of an overflowing bag of things you cannot use.

stoneford.belief: A sound crossing is our offering to people we will never meet.
stoneford.place: Masonry and roadside trade sustain Stoneford. Its lanes gather travelers before they head into rougher country.
stoneford.title: The crossing ward
stoneford.voice: Stay on the approaches near a crossing. A shortcut through the bank can be longer than the road.

stonehearth.belief: A place beside the hearth is offered before a stranger is asked for a story.
stonehearth.place: Compact stone homes and shared hearths give travelers a resting place among the eastern hills. Stores are kept close to the houses.
stonehearth.title: The shelter on the road
stonehearth.voice: Fill your food bag before you leave. The country beyond our lamps is not a town square.

willowcross.belief: We remember the hands that planted and harvested before ours.
willowcross.place: Fields, kitchens and timber work support the nearby roads. Willowcross measures a good season in full stores and repaired homes.
willowcross.title: The working village
willowcross.voice: Wood is shelter before it is fuel. Leave the paths clear when you work among the trees.
